q1_issues.issue: The matrix equative clause "This is the something ..." is entirely unparsed - no witness or atom for the subject "This" and no atom identifying it with the overlooked thing, so the sentence's main predication is missing.

The referent is typed with the pronoun itself, (Member sk_something_1 something), rather than a real kind such as thing, against the rule that a bare pronoun's witness is minted from its class and never from the pronoun.

q2_gaps: equative / identificational copular clause ("This is the N that ...") - Categorical statements covers only "X is a/an N" and "X is ADJ", not an identity between two referring expressions
demonstrative pronoun ("this" / "that") as a clause subject - the no-antecedent pronoun rule enumerates only he / she / they / it

finite restrictive relative clause on a head noun whose own subject is quantified ("the something many people seem to overlook") - only participial reduced relatives and universal "everyone who ..." rules are given, so nothing says whether to emit a distributing rule and how to link it back to the head noun
notes: The relative-clause half is well handled: "many" -> rule strength 0.7 with its QuantifierPhrase companion, and "seem" -> the epistemic Probably route, both as the instruction set specifies. The defect is that the clause the sentence is actually asserting was dropped.
